how_to_use: Start with the guide chapters in order. Complete the SAQ selector worksheet, then the scope inventory, then the readiness log. Use the incident-response one-pager and service-provider list templates as you go. Keep everything in one folder and review the renewal calendar monthly.
limitations: This kit does not determine your SAQ type, does not validate any control, and does not substitute for advice from your acquirer, a qualified assessor, or legal counsel. Requirements change over time; verify current expectations with your acquirer. Illustrative examples in the guide are simplified teaching cases, not assessments of any real business.
long_description: A plain-language readiness kit for US small merchants that accept card payments. It includes an SAQ selector decision-tree worksheet, a scope inventory and scope-reduction planner, a per-requirement readiness log with status formulas, an incident-response plan template, a service-provider list, an acquirer confirmation letter draft, and an attestation and renewal calendar. Every step is written for owners and office managers with no security background. Worked illustrative examples show how a retail shop, a food outlet, and a services firm would use each tool. The kit helps you build an organized file to discuss with your acquirer; it does not decide your SAQ path or attest on your behalf.
name: PCI SAQ Readiness Kit for Small Merchants
outcome_statement: Build an organized, reviewable readiness file: a documented candidate SAQ path, a scope inventory with reduction actions, a tracked readiness log, a posted incident plan, and a renewal calendar you can maintain year after year.
problem_statement: Small merchants face confusion over which PCI SAQ applies, scope creep toward the heavy SAQ D path, failed attestations, and breach liability. Multiple SAQ types exist for different environments, and small details such as an old laptop, emailed reports, or website handling can widen scope. MFA gaps and missing incident plans are common findings.
short_description: A plain-language kit that helps US small merchants pick a candidate SAQ path, shrink card-data scope, and prepare an organized attestation file.
support: Email support for file-access and how-to-use questions. Scope and questionnaire-path questions should go to your acquirer or bank, which decide what is required.
whats_included: Workbook with 5 sheets: SAQ selector worksheet, scope inventory, readiness log with status formulas, incident-plan checklist, renewal calendar
3 document templates: incident response one-pager, service-provider list, acquirer confirmation letter draft
Scope-reduction planner inside the guide and workbook
Renewal calendar with frequencies and overdue tracking
